title: 2019 Sonrisa Solar Park PPA: EDPR CA Solar Park VI LLC / East Bay Community Energy Authority
annotation_status: Assistant source-checked development labels; independent human review pending.
notes: Attachment 15C is the real, publicly disclosed 2019 execution-version PPA, spanning 123 pages including exhibits. The source is a 139-page July 2025 board packet.
Index only original PDF pages 9-131. Do not use the 2025 staff report or slides to fill redacted 2019 contract terms. This is not an evaluation of a newly negotiated 2025 agreement.
All page numbers are 1-based physical pages in the unmodified downloaded file. Cover sheet page 1 is PDF page 9; body page 1 is PDF page 16; payment page 38 is PDF page 53.

Some redacted pages were flattened into images. PDF page 53 contains readable payment text visually but only a filing header in PyMuPDF extraction. This challenge is retained, not removed to improve scores.
Q15 is unanswerable from the public copy because the numerical tariff is redacted. Its page points to the redaction, not an answer; exclude Q15 from retrieval hit-rate denominators.

This hand-selected single-document set is for development. Do not claim held-out or production accuracy. Exact field checks cover contract type, effective date and delivery-term years; all other fields require semantic review.
Public source PDF is downloaded into ignored data/, not redistributed with the evaluation set. Reference answers are paraphrases. Redacted content is never reconstructed.

questions.question: Who are the buyer and seller in this power purchase agreement?
questions.answer: Buyer: East Bay Community Energy Authority. Seller: EDPR CA Solar Park VI LLC.

questions.question: What is the effective date of this agreement?
How many contract years does the delivery term last?
What event starts the delivery term?
questions.answer: Commercial operation starts it, subject to early termination.

questions.question: What are the contracted battery storage power, discharge duration and energy output?
After notice of compliance costs above the cap following a change in law, how long does the buyer have to decide, and what choices does it have?
questions.answer: 60 days: reimburse agreed excess costs or waive the corresponding compliance actions.

questions.question: When must the buyer reimburse accepted compliance costs after receiving the seller's invoice and supporting documents?
What happens if the seller fails the guaranteed energy production requirement after contractual excuses and deemed deliveries are taken into account?
questions.answer: The seller owes damages determined under Exhibit G.

questions.question: Does making the contract unprofitable qualify as force majeure?
Does a continuing force majeure event excuse payments already due?
After how long can the non-claiming party terminate for force majeure, and what additional time can the seller receive after commercial operation?
questions.answer: After 12 consecutive months of relief; the seller may obtain six more months subject to the specified diligence, restoration-plan and evidence conditions.

questions.question: Following a continuing event of default, what date range may the non-defaulting party choose in its early termination notice?
questions.answer: From receipt of notice through 20 days thereafter.

questions.question: Under the general assignment rule, is the other party's consent needed and may that consent be unreasonably withheld?
questions.answer: Prior written consent is required and cannot be unreasonably withheld; separate exceptions apply.

questions.question: When must the buyer pay undisputed monthly invoices, and what happens if the due date falls on a weekend or legal holiday?
questions.answer: 30 days after invoice receipt or billing-month end, whichever is later; a weekend or holiday moves payment to the next business day.
questions.notes: Visually verified on the PDF image. PyMuPDF does not extract this clause; do not insert gold text into the retrieval index.

questions.question: What is the exact numerical renewable energy tariff per MWh in this public contract?
questions.answer: Not found in the public contract: the numerical rate is redacted.

parties.rubric: Identify EDPR CA Solar Park VI LLC as seller and East Bay Community Energy Authority as buyer. Do not substitute a party from the 2025 staff report.

effective_date.rubric: Use the 2019 preamble date, not the 2025 filing or meeting date.

term_years.rubric: 20 is the delivery term from COD; total time from the Effective Date also includes development.

COD.rubric: No specific scheduled or actual date is disclosed on the cover sheet. A partial value may explain that guaranteed COD equals expected COD as extended by the development cure period. Reject invented dates, including the 2025 report's proposed date.

price_tariff.rubric: Numerical renewable and storage rates are redacted. Accept explicit abstention or a qualified partial description with amount null. Do not accept an invented price or confuse a damage amount with the energy rate. Page 83 requires visual/OCR reading.

escalation.rubric: No general escalation percentage is disclosed. Accept abstention or a narrowly qualified description of the visible tax-credit non-adjustment provision; reject an invented percentage or a blanket claim that all price adjustments are prohibited.

delivery_point.rubric: Article 1 refers to Exhibit A; the specific delivery point in Exhibit A is redacted. Accept abstention or that qualified statement. Do not equate the project's county with the delivery point.

guaranteed_output.rubric: Distinguish 100 MW guaranteed generating capacity from energy production in MWh and the 30 MW/120 MWh storage contract. Energy-production percentage and storage-availability threshold are redacted. Preserve stated excuses and deemed/lost output if describing the production obligation. Do not invent annual GWh or guarantee percentages.

termination_rights.rubric: Describe continuing-default termination by notice (receipt through 20 days), and force-majeure termination after 12 months of relief, with the conditional six-month seller extension after COD. A complete pass requires both and no contradictory timing.

liquidated_damages.rubric: Distinguish the Damage Payment for seller default before COD (subject to 11.7) from the Termination Payment for other defaults under 11.3. Damage Payment equals development security; numerical amounts are redacted. Do not invent daily damages or caps.

change_in_law.rubric: Explain the compliance expenditure cap (amount redacted), notice of excess costs, buyer's 60-day choice to reimburse agreed excess costs or waive relevant actions, and reimbursement within 60 days of invoice plus documentation. Do not say all changes automatically increase tariff.

force_majeure.rubric: Preserve reasonable-efforts, control, fault/negligence conditions, the exclusion for unfavorable economics, and continuation of payments. A list of disasters alone is insufficient.

payment_terms.rubric: Undisputed invoices: wire or ACH within 30 days after invoice receipt or prior billing-period end, whichever is later; next business day for weekend/legal holiday. Late payments incur interest, but the numerical rate is redacted. Null is a miss: the clause is visible in the PDF despite missing extracted text.
